answer: The sonnet graph is rebuilt each epoch, and thus the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the kernel audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 8 times its size, so a group of 58 keys loses far more than 58 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the reef checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
